text:
maria: Ran a 24h synthetic fuzz suite targeting KV cache fragmentation + reuse under mixed long/short contexts. interleaved seq lengths: 64 / 12k / 512 / 8k. results look noisy, attaching summary and a tiny repro config. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: TL;DR: steady memory growth on some runs (~200MB over 6h), eviction spikes causing latency P99 jumps, reuse rate drops after long context switches. not all seeds fail.

maria: repro config (very small):
```yaml
workload: interleaved
seed: 42
pattern: [64, 12000, 512, 8000]
qps: 30
duration: 8h
kv_options:
  compaction_interval_ms: 60000
  eviction_policy: lru
  max_memory_mb: 4096
```

derek: thanks, can you paste the perf counters? especially fragment_count + max_free_chain_len.

maria: pasted a short table from perf output:
fragment_count: 1278
max_free_chain_len: 2048
reuse_rate: 0.62 -> 0.31 after 3rd hour
evictions/sec (spike): 45 -> baseline 2

asha: that reuse drop is suspicious. is KV compaction running on the same thread as kernel selection? we had a ticket where async compaction blocked batching heuristics.

maria: good point. i instrumented threads: compaction runs on background GC thread, kernel selector runs on inference worker. but we saw contention on the allocator lock. locking histogram attached (short):
alloc_lock_hold_ms: p50=0.3 p95=12.6 p99=90

jon: 90ms hold time could explain p99 blips. if alloc holds block KV reuse, you get fragmentation and new allocations leading to more evictions.

sam: did you try bumping compaction_interval_ms down to force more frequent compaction? might reduce free-chain length but could increase CPU.

maria: quick experiments: compaction 60s (baseline) vs 15s vs disabled. 15s reduced max_free_chain_len to ~512 and reuse rate stabilized at 0.6, but CPU rose ~8%. disabling compaction made fragmentation worse.

perf-bot: perf-regression-checker: baseline vs current branch: p99 latency regression detected on long-context workload (+18%), heap growth pattern differs. tag: perf/kv-frag-2028-03-04.

derek: what about kernel selection? if we change kernel to smaller-kernel mode for long contexts it might use less working set and reduce cache pressure. any logs about kernel switches during those runs?

maria: yes — saw frequent kernel swaps when seq_len > 8192. swap_count ~ 1.2 per request for long chunks. each swap triggers temporary KV allocs for rematerialized KVs.

asha: can we test a heuristic: pin kernel per-request to "long" if upcoming tokens > 8k, and avoid mid-request swaps? create a microbenchmark: single request with 12k tokens vs interleaved pattern.

maria: ran that microbenchmark. pinned-kernel reduced swap_count to 0.02 per request and reduced evictions by ~70% on that axis. but end-to-end latency for short requests increased slightly due to less optimal kernel for short segments.

jon: sounds like a routing/batching heuristic problem. we could add a preference to the batcher: group long requests together and apply pinned kernel scheduling. add a fallback for mixed batches.

sam: action items?

maria: proposed list:
- create a deterministic repro harness (seeded interleaved pattern) and add to long-context regression suite.
- add a perf test measuring fragment_count, max_free_chain_len, reuse_rate, alloc_lock_hold_ms, swap_count across 12h runs.
- prototype pinned-kernel scheduler and compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
- tune compaction_interval heuristic: make it workload-aware (more frequent after large long-context bursts).

derek: +1. also add alerting on eviction_spike_rate > 10/min during soak.

infra-bot: scheduled job created: perf/kv-frag-soak-1849126780 (8h -> 24h), owners: @maria, @derek. logs://internal/perf/1849126780

maria: i'll upload the full perf trace and heap profiles to the ticket. leaving notes in the regression repo. thanks for eyeballs :eyes:

sam: assign to eng-runtime backlog with P1 flaky perf tag.

jon: if anyone wants to help on the pinned-kernel prototype ping me, i'll pair on the scheduler.

maria: on it, will open a PR with the repro harness and a draft perf test by EOD.

perf-bot: note: include deterministic seeds and CI flags to opt into long-run tests so we don't block normal CI.

maria: agreed. final note: this only repros reliably with interleaved patterns (long-short-long) not pure long streams. suggests reuse fragmentation happens on switches.

asha: perfect clue. that narrows root cause. i'll look at allocator freelist behavior during length transitions tomorrow.

maria: thanks all.
